| **Test Type** | Robustness / Timing |

**Preconditions:**
- Nominal conditions (25 °C, 13.5 V, < 10% bus load)
- SW module configured to issue **10 rapid consecutive send requests** with < 1 ms interval (burst scenario)

**Test Steps:**

| Step | Action | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Trigger burst of 10 consecutive send requests from SW module | GPIO toggles observed for each request |
| 2 | Capture corresponding CAN frame timestamps | Correct CAN frames with correct IDs observed |
| 3 | Calculate L for each frame | All values logged |
| 4 | Repeat burst 10 times (total 100 measurements) | All measurements captured |
| 5 | Evaluate max(L) < 50 ms | **PASS** if all L < 50 ms |
| 6 | Verify no CAN frames are lost or duplicated | Frame count = 100 |

**Pass/Fail Criteria:**

| Metric | Acceptance Threshold |
|---|---|
| Maximum latency | **< 50 ms** |
| Violations | **0** |
| Lost frames | **0** |
| Duplicate frames | **0** |

---

## 8. Measurement Uncertainty and Timing Budget

To ensure compliance with ISO 26262 rigor, the measurement uncertainty shall be characterized and accounted for.

| Source | Estimated Uncertainty | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Logic analyzer timestamp resolution | ± 1 µs | Negligible |
| GPIO toggle overhead (instrumentation) | < 1 ms | Subtract from measurement if > 0.5 ms |
| CAN bus synchronization delay | < 0.5 µs | Negligible |
| Temperature-induced clock drift | < 100 ppm | Negligible |
| **Total Measurement Uncertainty** | **< 2 ms** | **Conservative guard band applied** |

> **Guard Band:** To account for measurement uncertainty, the **effective acceptance threshold used during testing shall be 48 ms** (50 ms − 2 ms guard band). Any latency **between 48 ms and 50 ms** shall be flagged for engineering review even if technically within limit.

---

## 9. Entry and Exit Criteria

### 9.1 Entry Criteria
- [ ] Approved Test Plan and Test Specification (this document)
- [ ] HU SW build available, reviewed, and baselined in version control
- [ ] Test environment set up, calibrated, and verified
- [ ] All required test equipment calibration certificates valid
- [ ] No open safety-critical defects (ASIL B or above) in DUT
- [ ] Measurement instrumentation characterized (overhead < 1 ms verified)

### 9.2 Exit Criteria
- [ ] All 8 test cases executed (100% coverage of REQ-CAN-HU-001)
- [ ] All test cases result in **PASS**
- [ ] Test results reviewed and approved by safety engineer
- [ ] Test report generated and archived
- [ ] All deviations and anomalies documented and resolved or accepted with rationale

---

## 10. Defect Classification

| Severity | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical (S1)** | Any latency ≥ 50 ms observed | Immediate stop; raise safety defect; root cause analysis required |
| **Major (S2)** | Latency between 48 ms and < 50 ms | Flag for engineering review; regression test required |
| **Minor (S3)** | Mean latency increase ≥ 20% vs baseline | Document and monitor |
| **Observation** | Any anomaly not affecting latency requirement | Log for future reference |

---

## 11. Traceability Matrix

| Test Case ID | Requirement ID | Test Type | Operating Condition | ASIL Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-CAN-HU-001 | REQ-CAN-HU-001 | Nominal | 25 °C / 13.5 V / Low BusLoad | ASIL B |
| TC-CAN-HU-002 | REQ-CAN-HU-001 | Stress | 25 °C / 13.5 V / High BusLoad | ASIL B |
| TC-CAN-HU-003 | REQ-CAN-HU-001 | Stress | 25 °C / 13.5 V / High CPU Load | ASIL B |
| TC-CAN-HU-004 | REQ-CAN-HU-001 | Boundary | 25 °C / 9.0 V / Low BusLoad | ASIL B |
| TC-CAN-HU-005 | REQ-CAN-HU-001 | Boundary | 25 °C / 16.0 V / Low BusLoad | ASIL B |
| TC-CAN-HU-006 | REQ-CAN-HU-001 | Environmental | −40 °C / 13.5 V / Low BusLoad | ASIL B |
| TC-CAN-HU-007 | REQ-CAN-HU-001 | Environmental | +85 °C / 13.5 V / Low BusLoad | ASIL B |
| TC-CAN-HU-008 | REQ-CAN-HU-001 | Robustness | 25 °C / 13.5 V / Burst | ASIL B |

**Requirement Coverage: 100%** (REQ-CAN-HU-001 covered by 8 test cases)

---

## 12. Test Report Requirements

The test report shall include:

1. **Test summary** – pass/fail status per test case
2. **Raw measurement data** – all latency values (L) per test case in MDF4/CSV format
3. **Statistical analysis** – min, max, mean, standard deviation per test case
4. **Worst-case identification** – identification of the worst-case operating condition
5. **Instrumentation overhead report** – documented overhead and correction applied
6. **Deviation log** – any deviations from this specification with justification
7. **Safety engineer sign-off** – approval signature with date
8. **Traceability confirmation** – confirmation of 100% requirement coverage

---

## 13. Approval and Sign-Off

| Role | Name | Signature | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Test Engineer | | | |
| Safety Engineer (FuSa) | | | |
| Software Architect | | | |
| System Engineer | | | |
| Quality Manager | | | |

*This document shall be maintained under configuration management and updated upon any change to REQ-CAN-HU-001 or the HU CAN Interface design.*

**"Operational System shall verify information from other Vehicle Systems before sending it to Center Display and B-Pillar Display"**

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement | ISO 26262 Reference |
|---|---|---|
| TR-001 | The system shall perform **range checks** on all received signals before forwarding to displays | Part 6, Clause 7.4.5 |
| TR-002 | The system shall perform **plausibility checks** against related signals to detect inconsistencies | Part 6, Clause 7.4.5 |
| TR-003 | The system shall validate signal **data types and formats** prior to transmission | Part 6, Clause 7.4.5 |

---

### 2. **Communication Integrity Verification**

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement | ISO 26262 Reference |
|---|---|---|
| TR-004 | The system shall verify **CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check)** of received messages from vehicle systems | Part 7, Clause 8 (E2E Protection) |
| TR-005 | The system shall verify **message counter/sequence numbers** to detect missing or repeated messages | Part 7, Clause 8 |
| TR-006 | The system shall implement **End-to-End (E2E) protection** per AUTOSAR E2E Profile for safety-relevant signals | Part 7, Clause 8.3 |
| TR-007 | The system shall detect **timeout/reception errors** when signals from vehicle systems are not received within defined time window | Part 7, Clause 8 |

---

### 3. **Signal Timeout & Alive Monitoring**

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement | ISO 26262 Reference |
|---|---|---|
| TR-008 | The system shall monitor signal **alive counters** to detect loss of communication from source vehicle systems | Part 7, Clause 8 |
| TR-009 | The system shall trigger a **safe state or substitute value** when a timeout is detected on safety-relevant signals | Part 4, Clause 8 (HARA) |
| TR-010 | Maximum tolerable **timeout window** shall be derived from FMEA/FTA and ASIL allocation | Part 9, Clause 8 |

---

### 4. **Substitute Value / Safe State Handling**

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement | ISO 26262 Reference |
|---|---|---|
| TR-011 | Upon detection of invalid data, the system shall substitute with a **defined default/safe value** or display an error indicator | Part 4, Clause 8.4 |
| TR-012 | The substitute value strategy shall ensure the **displayed information does not mislead the driver** | Part 4 (HARA), Part 3 |
| TR-013 | The system shall **notify the driver** (via display or warning) when substituted/degraded data is being shown | Part 4, Clause 8 |

---

### 5. **ASIL Decomposition & Freedom from Interference**

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement | ISO 26262 Reference |
|---|---|---|
| TR-014 | The verification mechanism shall be assigned the **appropriate ASIL level** consistent with the HARA outcome | Part 4, Clause 8 |
| TR-015 | The system shall ensure **freedom from interference** between safety-relevant and non-safety-relevant signal paths | Part 6, Clause 7.4.7 |
| TR-016 | If ASIL decomposition is applied, each sub-element shall maintain its assigned **ASIL(x)D** integrity | Part 9, Clause 5 |

---

### 6. **Fault Detection & Diagnostic Coverage**

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement | ISO 26262 Reference |
|---|---|---|
| TR-017 | The system shall implement **diagnostic monitoring** with sufficient coverage (DC) per FMEA | Part 5, Clause 8 (hardware) |
| TR-018 | Detected faults shall be **logged to DTC (Diagnostic Trouble Codes)** for traceability | Part 6, Clause 7 |
| TR-019 | The system shall achieve the required **PMHF (Probabilistic Metric for Hardware Failure)** target | Part 5, Clause 9 |

---

### 7. **Latency & Timing Requirements**

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement | ISO 26262 Reference |
|---|---|---|
| TR-020 | Verification shall be completed within the **defined FTTI (Fault Tolerant Time Interval)** | Part 4, Clause 8 |
| TR-021 | The system shall detect and respond to invalid data within the **maximum reaction time** derived from FTTI | Part 4, Clause 8.4 |

---

## Summary: Key ISO 26262 Mechanisms Applied

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Vehicle System  →  [Verification Layer]  →  Displays   │
│                                                          │
│  Verification Layer performs:                           │
│  ✅ E2E Protection (CRC + Counter)                      │
│  ✅ Range & Plausibility Checks                         │
│  ✅ Timeout / Alive Monitoring                          │

## Applicable ASIL Considerations

# Test Procedure: VM RTOS Functional Verification

**ASIL Level:** [Define per project]

## Test Procedure

### TP-VM-RTOS-001-01: Task Scheduling Verification

| Step | Action | Expected Result | Pass/Fail |
|------|--------|-----------------|-----------|
| 1 | Initialize the VM RTOS environment and power on the target hardware | System boots without errors; RTOS kernel initializes successfully | |
| 2 | Create three tasks with different priorities (High, Medium, Low) | All three tasks are created and registered in the RTOS task list | |
| 3 | Trigger all three tasks simultaneously | High-priority task executes first, followed by Medium, then Low | |
| 4 | Verify task preemption by activating a High-priority task while Low-priority task is running | Low-priority task is preempted; High-priority task takes CPU control immediately | |
| 5 | Record CPU execution order via trace tool | Execution order matches defined priority levels without deviation | |

---

### TP-VM-RTOS-001-02: Task Timing and Deadline Verification

| Step | Action | Expected Result | Pass/Fail |
|------|--------|-----------------|-----------|
| 1 | Configure a periodic task with a defined cycle time (e.g., 10 ms) | Task is registered with the correct period | |
| 2 | Start the periodic task and run for 1000 cycles | Task executes every 10 ms ± defined jitter tolerance | |
| 3 | Measure task activation timestamps using hardware timer or oscilloscope | All measured periods are within the defined tolerance window | |
| 4 | Introduce a CPU load of 80% and re-measure task timing | Task deadlines are still met; no missed deadlines are observed | |
| 5 | Log and evaluate timing data against requirements | All cycle times conform to the specified timing requirement | |

---

### TP-VM-RTOS-001-03: Inter-Task Communication Verification

| Step | Action | Expected Result | Pass/Fail |
|------|--------|-----------------|-----------|
| 1 | Configure Task A as sender and Task B as receiver using a defined IPC mechanism (e.g., message queue, event flag) | IPC channel is created without errors | |
| 2 | Task A sends a predefined data message to Task B | Message is placed in the queue without error | |
| 3 | Task B receives and reads the message | Received data matches the sent data exactly | |
| 4 | Repeat the communication 1000 times | No data corruption, loss, or duplication is observed | |
| 5 | Verify mutual exclusion by using a shared resource between two tasks with a semaphore/mutex | No race condition or data inconsistency is detected | |

---

### TP-VM-RTOS-001-04: Resource Management Verification

| Step | Action | Expected Result | Pass/Fail |
|------|--------|-----------------|-----------|
| 1 | Allocate maximum defined memory resources within the VM RTOS | Memory is allocated successfully without overflow | |
| 2 | Release allocated resources | Resources are returned to the pool correctly; no memory leak is detected | |
| 3 | Attempt to allocate resources beyond defined limits | RTOS returns an error code; no system crash or undefined behavior occurs | |
| 4 | Verify stack usage of all tasks under maximum load | Stack usage does not exceed defined limits for any task | |

---

### TP-VM-RTOS-001-05: Error Handling and Safety Mechanism Verification

| Step | Action | Expected Result | Pass/Fail |
|------|--------|-----------------|-----------|
| 1 | Inject a stack overflow condition in a low-priority task | RTOS detects the overflow and triggers the defined error handler | |
| 2 | Simulate a watchdog timeout by blocking the main task | Watchdog triggers a system reset or safe state as defined | |
| 3 | Force an illegal memory access from a task | RTOS isolates the faulting task and reports the error; other tasks continue execution | |
| 4 | Simulate VM partition failure | RTOS detects partition failure and enforces isolation; no cross-partition corruption occurs | |
| 5 | Verify that the system transitions to a safe state | System enters the predefined safe state within the defined response time | |

---

### TP-VM-RTOS-001-06: VM Partition Isolation Verification

| Step | Action | Expected Result | Pass/Fail |
|------|--------|-----------------|-----------|
| 1 | Configure two VM partitions (Safety partition and QM partition) | Both partitions initialize independently | |
| 2 | Trigger a fault condition in the QM partition | Safety partition continues to operate without interruption | |
| 3 | Attempt to access Safety partition memory from QM partition | Access is denied; memory protection violation is reported | |
| 4 | Verify temporal isolation by loading QM partition to 100% CPU | Safety-critical tasks in the Safety partition maintain timing | |

---

## Test Completion Criteria

|----------|-------------|
| **Pass Criteria** | All test steps produce expected results with no deviations |
| **Fail Criteria** | Any step produces an unexpected result or system behaves outside defined parameters |
| **Regression** | All failed test cases must be re-executed after defect resolution |

text: ISO 26262 Verification of risk assessment
answer:
# ISO 26262 Verification of Risk Assessment

## Overview

ISO 26262 requires systematic verification of risk assessments to ensure that **Automotive Safety Integrity Levels (ASIL)** are correctly assigned and that safety goals adequately address identified hazards.

---

## 1. Risk Assessment Framework

### Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment (HARA)
The risk assessment is based on three parameters:

| Parameter | Description | Levels |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| **Severity (S)** | Harm to persons | S0 – S3 |
| **Exposure (E)** | Frequency of hazardous situation | E0 – E4 |
| **Controllability (C)** | Driver/operator ability to control | C0 – C3 |

### ASIL Determination
```
ASIL = f(Severity, Exposure, Controllability)
```
Results in: **QM, ASIL A, ASIL B, ASIL C, ASIL D**

---

## 2. Verification Objectives

### Key Questions to Verify
- ✅ Are all operational situations and hazardous events identified?
- ✅ Are S, E, C ratings justified and documented?
- ✅ Are ASIL assignments correct per the classification table?
- ✅ Are safety goals complete, verifiable, and unambiguous?
- ✅ Is ASIL decomposition properly justified?

---

## 3. Verification Methods

### 3.1 Review & Inspection
- **Independent Review** — Subject matter experts review HARA outputs
- **Checklist-Based Inspection** — Structured verification against ISO 26262 Part 3 requirements
- **Peer Review** — Cross-functional team validation

### 3.2 Walkthrough
- Step-by-step examination of hazard identification process
- Scenario-based discussion with safety team

### 3.3 Formal Methods (for high ASIL)
- Mathematical verification of classification logic
- Consistency checks across related safety analyses

---

## 4. Verification Checklist

### Hazard Identification
```
☐ All vehicle operating modes considered
☐ Environmental conditions addressed
☐ Driver/passenger/pedestrian exposure considered
☐ Foreseeable misuse scenarios included
☐ Item boundary and interfaces defined
```

### Severity Rating Verification
```
☐ S0 – No injuries justified
☐ S1 – Light/moderate injuries justified
☐ S2 – Severe/life-threatening (survival probable) justified
☐ S3 – Life-threatening (survival uncertain)/fatal justified
☐ Referenced accident data or field experience
```

### Exposure Rating Verification
```
☐ E0 – Incredible frequency justified
☐ E1 – Very low probability justified
☐ E2 – Low probability justified
☐ E3 – Medium probability justified
☐ E4 – High probability justified
☐ Statistical data or engineering judgment documented
```

### Controllability Rating Verification
```
☐ C0 – Controllable in general justified
☐ C1 – Simply controllable justified
☐ C2 – Normally controllable justified
☐ C3 – Difficult to control/uncontrollable justified
☐ Human factors analysis referenced
```

---

## 5. Common Verification Findings

### Typical Defects Found
| Defect Type | Example | Risk |
|-------------|---------|------|
| **Under-rating Severity** | S2 assigned instead of S3 | ASIL too low → insufficient safety measures |
| **Under-rating Exposure** | E2 instead of E4 | ASIL too low |
| **Over-rating Controllability** | C1 instead of C3 | ASIL too low |
| **Missing hazard scenarios** | Partial loss not considered | Unmitigated risk |
| **Vague safety goals** | Non-verifiable statements | Inadequate verification |
| **Incorrect ASIL decomposition** | Improper independence | Invalid risk reduction |

---

## 6. Verification Evidence Requirements

### Documentation Required
```
1. HARA Report with rationale for each rating
2. Minutes of review meetings
3. Review checklists (completed & signed)
4. Traceability matrix (Hazard → Safety Goal → ASIL)
5. Deviation reports and resolutions
6. Sign-off by qualified safety engineer
```

---

## 7. Independence Requirements

| ASIL Level | Required Independence |
|------------|----------------------|
| **QM** | Not required |
| **ASIL A** | Independent person (I1) |
| **ASIL B** | Independent person (I1) |
| **ASIL C** | Independent department (I2) |
| **ASIL D** | Independent organization (I3) |

---

## 8. Verification Process Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│         HARA Draft Complete         │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
               │
               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│    Internal Consistency Check       │
│  (S, E, C ratings vs. ASIL table)  │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
               │
               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│    Independent Technical Review     │
│    (per ASIL independence level)    │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
               │
         ┌─────┴─────┐
         │           │
      Pass         Fail
         │           │
         ▼           ▼
   ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
   │ Approved │  │ Issue Report │
   │  HARA    │  │  & Rework    │
   └──────────┘  └──────┬───────┘
                        │
                        └──► Re-verification
```

---

## 9. Key Standards References

| Document | Content |
|----------|---------|
| **ISO 26262-3** | Concept phase — HARA requirements |
| **ISO 26262-2** | Management of functional safety |
| **ISO 26262-8** | Supporting processes (verification) |
| **ISO 26262-9** | ASIL-oriented and safety-oriented analyses |

---

## 10. Best Practices

> 💡 **Use multiple scenarios** — Test edge cases and worst-case combinations
>
> 💡 **Cross-functional team** — Include systems, SW, HW, safety, and validation engineers
>
> 💡 **Traceability** — Every safety goal must trace to a verified hazard
>
> 💡 **Living document** — Re-verify when system changes occur
>
> 💡 **Benchmarking** — Compare with similar vehicle systems/industry databases

---

## Summary

Verification of risk assessment in ISO 26262 ensures that:
1. **All hazards are identified** systematically
2. **ASIL assignments are correct** and justified
3. **Safety goals are complete** and verifiable
4. **Independence requirements** are met
5. **Evidence is documented** for functional safety audit/assessment

text: ISO 26262:  Test Specification for a functional requirement "HMI-Center-Display shall be able to receive data from HMI-Driver-Display and show it on the CID". Write only a Test Procedure.

# Test Specification – Test Procedure

**Requirement ID:** HMI-REQ-XXX
**Requirement:** HMI-Center-Display shall be able to receive data from HMI-Driver-Display and show it on the CID
**Test Case ID:** TC-HMI-CID-001

---

## Test Procedure

### Pre-conditions
- HMI-Center-Display (CID) is powered ON and in operational state
- HMI-Driver-Display is powered ON and in operational state
- Communication link between HMI-Driver-Display and HMI-Center-Display is established
- System is initialized and no active fault/DTC is present
- Test equipment (signal analyzer / diagnostic tool) is connected

---

### Test Steps

| Step No. | Action | Expected Result | Pass / Fail |
|----------|--------|-----------------|-------------|
| 1 | Power ON the HMI-Driver-Display and HMI-Center-Display (CID) | Both displays initialize successfully without error messages | |
| 2 | Verify the communication link is active between HMI-Driver-Display and HMI-Center-Display | Communication bus is active; no communication fault is reported | |
| 3 | On HMI-Driver-Display, generate/trigger **Dataset-1** (e.g., speed value = 80 km/h) to be transmitted to CID | Dataset-1 is sent from HMI-Driver-Display over the communication interface | |
| 4 | Observe the CID screen and verify that Dataset-1 is displayed correctly | CID displays the received data (speed = 80 km/h) accurately and without distortion | |
| 5 | On HMI-Driver-Display, update the data to **Dataset-2** (e.g., speed value = 120 km/h) | Updated Dataset-2 is transmitted from HMI-Driver-Display to CID | |
| 6 | Observe the CID screen and verify that Dataset-2 is displayed correctly | CID updates and displays the new received data (speed = 120 km/h) accurately | |
| 7 | Verify the data update latency between HMI-Driver-Display transmission and CID display | Data is displayed on CID within the defined maximum latency (e.g., ≤ XXX ms as per system requirement) | |
| 8 | Introduce a **temporary communication interruption** between HMI-Driver-Display and CID (e.g., disconnect bus for 2 seconds) | CID detects communication loss and shows defined fail-safe behavior (e.g., last valid data retained or warning displayed) | |
| 9 | Restore the communication link between HMI-Driver-Display and CID | Communication is re-established; CID resumes receiving and displaying updated data correctly | |
| 10 | On HMI-Driver-Display, transmit **boundary value data** (e.g., minimum and maximum data range values) | CID correctly receives and displays both boundary values without overflow, truncation, or incorrect rendering | |
| 11 | Verify no DTCs or error codes are logged during normal data transmission | No unexpected DTCs or errors are recorded in the system | |
| 12 | Power OFF HMI-Driver-Display while CID is active | CID detects the absence of data source and responds per defined fail-safe behavior (e.g., display warning or last valid value) | |

---

### Post-conditions
- System is restored to its initial operational state
- All test data and observations are recorded
- Any DTCs generated during testing are documented and cleared (if applicable)

---

### Pass / Fail Criteria

| Criteria | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| **PASS** | All expected results in Steps 1–12 are met; CID correctly receives, processes, and displays data from HMI-Driver-Display under all tested conditions |
| **FAIL** | Any step produces a result deviating from the expected result; data is missing, incorrectly displayed, exceeds latency limit, or fail-safe behavior is not triggered appropriately |

---

### References
- ISO 26262-6: Product Development at the Software Level
- System Architecture Specification – HMI Communication Interface
- HMI Display Software Requirement Specification

text: ISO 26262:  Test Specification for a functional requirement "HMI-Driver-Display shall be able to notice if Drivetrain System turns on or off functions and show an information message on driver display". Write only a Test Procedure.
answer:
# Test Specification: HMI Driver Display – Drivetrain System Function Notification

## Test Procedure

---

### TP-HMI-DD-001: Drivetrain System Function Turn ON Notification

**Test Procedure Steps:**

| Step | Action | Expected Result | Pass/Fail |
|------|--------|-----------------|-----------|
| 1 | Set up the test environment: Connect HMI-Driver-Display unit to Drivetrain System via communication bus (CAN/Ethernet) | All communication links established; no DTCs present | |
| 2 | Power ON the vehicle system and verify HMI-Driver-Display is in normal operational state | Display shows default/home screen; no active drivetrain messages visible | |
| 3 | Verify baseline state: Confirm all Drivetrain System functions are in OFF state | No drivetrain function information messages displayed on driver display | |
| 4 | Trigger Drivetrain System to activate **Function #1** (e.g., Traction Control) via test tool/signal injection | Drivetrain System transmits "Function ON" signal on the communication bus | |
| 5 | Monitor communication bus and capture signal transmission from Drivetrain System to HMI | Signal frame with correct identifier and payload (Function ON status) is detected within defined latency (e.g., ≤ 100 ms) | |
| 6 | Observe HMI-Driver-Display within defined response time | An information message is displayed on the driver display indicating the Drivetrain function has turned ON | |
| 7 | Verify message content and format | Message text, icon, or symbol correctly identifies the specific drivetrain function turned ON; conforms to UI specification | |
| 8 | Verify message display duration | Message remains visible for the defined duration as per HMI specification | |
| 9 | Log all signal timestamps and display events | Timestamps recorded; end-to-end latency within defined system requirement (e.g., ≤ 500 ms) | |
| 10 | Repeat Steps 4–9 for all defined Drivetrain System functions (Function #2, #3, … #N) | Each function activation correctly triggers a corresponding information message on the driver display | |

---

### TP-HMI-DD-002: Drivetrain System Function Turn OFF Notification

**Test Procedure Steps:**

| Step | Action | Expected Result | Pass/Fail |
|------|--------|-----------------|-----------|
| 1 | Set up the test environment: Connect HMI-Driver-Display unit to Drivetrain System via communication bus | All communication links established; no DTCs present | |
| 2 | Power ON the vehicle system and verify HMI-Driver-Display is in normal operational state | Display shows default/home screen | |
| 3 | Pre-condition: Trigger Drivetrain System to activate **Function #1** and confirm ON notification is displayed (as per TP-HMI-DD-001) | Function ON message is visible on driver display | |
| 4 | Trigger Drivetrain System to deactivate **Function #1** via test tool/signal injection | Drivetrain System transmits "Function OFF" signal on the communication bus | |
| 5 | Monitor communication bus and capture signal transmission from Drivetrain System to HMI | Signal frame with correct identifier and payload (Function OFF status) is detected within defined latency (e.g., ≤ 100 ms) | |
| 6 | Observe HMI-Driver-Display within defined response time | An information message is displayed on the driver display indicating the Drivetrain function has turned OFF | |
| 7 | Verify message content and format | Message text, icon, or symbol correctly identifies the specific drivetrain function turned OFF; conforms to UI specification | |
| 8 | Verify message display duration | Message remains visible for the defined duration as per HMI specification, then clears | |
| 9 | Log all signal timestamps and display events | Timestamps recorded; end-to-end latency within defined system requirement | |
| 10 | Repeat Steps 3–9 for all defined Drivetrain System functions (Function #2, #3, … #N) | Each function deactivation correctly triggers a corresponding information message on the driver display | |

---

### TP-HMI-DD-003: Rapid Consecutive ON/OFF State Change Notification

**Test Procedure Steps:**

| Step | Action | Expected Result | Pass/Fail |
|------|--------|-----------------|-----------|
| 1 | Set up test environment and confirm baseline operational state | System ready; no active drivetrain messages | |
| 2 | Trigger Drivetrain Function #1 ON, then immediately trigger OFF within a short interval (e.g., < 200 ms) via test tool | Both ON and OFF signals transmitted on the bus in rapid succession | |
| 3 | Observe HMI-Driver-Display behavior | Display handles state changes gracefully; no missing, frozen, or corrupted messages | |
| 4 | Verify that no message overlap or display error occurs | Messages are displayed sequentially or the latest state is shown, per system specification | |
| 5 | Repeat with multiple functions toggled simultaneously | HMI correctly processes and displays all concurrent drivetrain function notifications without loss | |

---

### TP-HMI-DD-004: Communication Bus Failure – HMI Notification Robustness

**Test Procedure Steps:**

| Step | Action | Expected Result | Pass/Fail |
|------|--------|-----------------|-----------|
| 1 | Set up test environment and confirm baseline operational state | System ready; communication bus active | |
| 2 | Simulate communication bus interruption between Drivetrain System and HMI-Driver-Display | Bus signal lost or degraded | |
| 3 | Trigger Drivetrain System to change function state (ON or OFF) during bus interruption | Signal cannot be delivered to HMI | |
| 4 | Observe HMI-Driver-Display | No false or erroneous drivetrain information message is displayed; system handles missing signal per fail-safe specification | |
| 5 | Restore communication bus | Bus communication re-established | |
| 6 | Trigger Drivetrain System to change function state again | HMI-Driver-Display correctly receives signal and displays appropriate information message | |

---

### Test Completion Criteria

| Criteria | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| **Pass Criteria** | All test steps produce expected results; all drivetrain function ON/OFF state changes result in correct information messages displayed on driver display within defined latency |
| **Fail Criteria** | Any missing, incorrect, delayed (beyond specification), or erroneous information message is observed on the driver display |
| **Anomaly Handling** | Any deviation shall be logged as a defect with step reference, signal trace, and screenshot/video evidence |

---

> **Note:** This test procedure is written in accordance with **ISO 26262-6** (Software Level Testing) and **ISO 26262-4** (System Level Testing) guidelines, targeting functional verification of the HMI-Driver-Display requirement at integration and system test levels.

text: write more about accessibility testing. does accessibility testing also include different screen sizes?
answer:
# Accessibility Testing ## What is Accessibility Testing? Accessibility testing is a type of software testing that ensures applications are **usable by people with disabilities** and meet established accessibility standards. The goal is to make sure no user is excluded from using your application regardless of their abilities. --- ## Types of Disabilities Addressed Accessibility testing covers users with: - **Visual impairments** – blindness, low vision, color blindness - **Hearing impairments** – deafness, hard of hearing - **Motor impairments** – limited hand mobility, tremors, paralysis - **Cognitive impairments** – dyslexia, ADHD, memory difficulties - **Neurological conditions** – epilepsy, autism spectrum --- ## Accessibility Standards & Guidelines The most widely used standard is **WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines)**, maintained by W3C. ### WCAG is built on 4 principles (POUR): | Principle | Meaning | |-----------|---------| | **Perceivable** | Users can perceive all content | | **Operable** | Users can operate all functionality | | **Understandable** | Content is easy to understand | | **Robust** | Works across different assistive technologies | ### Compliance Levels: - **Level A** – Minimum accessibility - **Level AA** – Standard requirement (most laws require this) - **Level AAA** – Highest level of accessibility --- ## What Accessibility Testing Actually Covers ### 1. 🖥️ Screen Reader Compatibility Testing whether screen readers can properly read and navigate your application. **Popular screen readers:** - **NVDA** (Windows – free) - **JAWS** (Windows – paid) - **VoiceOver** (macOS/iOS – built-in) - **TalkBack** (Android – built-in) **What to check:** ``` ✅ Images have descriptive alt text ✅ Form fields have proper labels ✅ Headings are in logical order (H1 → H2 → H3) ✅ Buttons have descriptive names (not just "click here") ✅ Error messages are announced by screen readers ✅ Dynamic content changes are announced ``` --- ### 2. ⌨️ Keyboard Navigation Many users cannot use a mouse and rely entirely on a keyboard. **What to check:** ``` ✅ All features are reachable using Tab key ✅ Focus order is logical and follows page flow ✅ Focus indicator is always visible ✅ No keyboard traps (user gets stuck) ✅ Dropdown menus work with arrow keys ✅ Modals/popups can be closed with Escape key ✅ Skip navigation links exist ``` **Example of a skip navigation link:** ```html Skip to main content ``` --- ### 3. 🎨 Color & Contrast **Color contrast ratio** ensures text is readable against its background. **WCAG requirements:** | Text Type | Minimum Contrast Ratio | |-----------|----------------------| | Normal text | 4.5:1 | | Large text (18pt+) | 3:1 | | UI components | 3:1 | **Other color checks:** ``` ✅ Information is NOT conveyed by color alone ✅ Error states use more than just red color ✅ Links are distinguishable from regular text ✅ Color blind users can understand all content ``` **Example - Bad vs Good:** ``` ❌ Bad: "Required fields are in red" ✅ Good: "Required fields are marked with * and highlighted" ``` --- ### 4. 📝 Forms & Input ``` ✅ Every input has a visible label ✅ Labels are programmatically associated with inputs ✅ Error messages are clear and descriptive ✅ Required fields are clearly indicated ✅ Autocomplete attributes are used correctly ✅ Timeout warnings give users enough time ``` **Example - Bad vs Good:** ```html ``` --- ### 5. 🎥 Media Accessibility ``` ✅ Videos have captions/subtitles ✅ Audio has transcripts ✅ Videos have audio descriptions for visual content ✅ Media players are keyboard accessible ✅ No content flashes more than 3 times per second (prevents seizures for epileptic users) ``` --- ### 6. 📄 Document Structure & Semantics ``` ✅ Proper HTML semantic elements used ✅ Page has a meaningful title ✅ Language is declared in HTML ✅ Landmarks are used correctly (header, nav, main, footer) ✅ Lists use proper ul/ol/li elements ✅ Tables have proper headers ``` **Example - Semantic HTML:** ```html
My App
Menu
Main content
My App
Menu
Main content
``` --- ## Does Accessibility Testing Include Different Screen Sizes? ### Short Answer: **Not directly — that is Responsive Design Testing** However, they **overlap significantly** and both are important. --- ### The Relationship Between Accessibility & Screen Sizes | Aspect | Accessibility Testing | Responsive Testing | |--------|----------------------|-------------------| | **Primary focus** | Disabilities & assistive tech | Screen sizes & devices | | **Standards** | WCAG guidelines | No fixed standard | | **Tools** | Screen readers, contrast checkers | Browser dev tools, real devices | | **Overlap area** | Mobile accessibility, zoom behavior | Touch targets, readable text | --- ### Where They Overlap #### 📱 Mobile Accessibility (Overlap Area) Mobile accessibility IS part of accessibility testing: ``` ✅ Touch targets are at least 44x44 pixels (WCAG requirement) ✅ Content is accessible on mobile screen readers (TalkBack/VoiceOver) ✅ Pinch-to-zoom is NOT disabled ✅ Content reflows at 320px wide (WCAG 1.4.10) ✅ Orientation is not locked (unless necessary) ``` **Important WCAG rule about zoom:** ```html ``` > Low vision users rely on browser zoom (up to 400%) to read content --- #### 🔍 Text Reflow (WCAG 1.4.10) When users zoom to 400%, content should **reflow** (not require horizontal scrolling). This is both an **accessibility requirement** AND a **responsive design concern**. --- ## Accessibility Testing Tools ### Automated Tools | Tool | Type | What it catches | |------|------|----------------| | **axe DevTools** | Browser extension | ~30% of issues | | **WAVE** | Browser extension | Visual feedback | | **Lighthouse** | Chrome built-in | Score + audit | | **Deque axe** | CI/CD integration | Automated testing | | **Siteimprove** | Platform | Ongoing monitoring | ### Manual Testing Tools | Tool | Purpose | |------|---------| | **Color Contrast Analyzer** | Check color ratios | | **NoCoffee Vision Simulator** | Simulate visual impairments | | **NVDA + Firefox** | Screen reader testing | | **VoiceOver + Safari** | Apple screen reader testing | --- ## Automated vs Manual Testing ``` Automated tools catch ~30% of accessibility issues Manual testing is required for the remaining ~70% ``` | Testing Type | Examples | |-------------|---------| | **Automated** | Missing alt text, color contrast, empty labels | | **Manual** | Logical reading order, meaningful link text, usability | | **User testing** | Testing with real users who have disabilities | --- ## Accessibility Testing Checklist Summary ``` STRUCTURE ✅ Page title is descriptive ✅ Heading hierarchy is correct ✅ Landmark regions exist ✅ Language is set IMAGES & MEDIA ✅ All images have alt text ✅ Decorative images have empty alt="" ✅ Videos have captions ✅ Audio has transcripts FORMS ✅ All inputs have labels ✅ Errors are clearly described ✅ Required fields are marked NAVIGATION ✅ Keyboard navigable ✅ Visible focus indicator ✅ Skip navigation link exists ✅ No keyboard traps VISUAL ✅ Color contrast passes WCAG ✅ Color is not only visual indicator ✅ Text resizable to 200% without loss MOBILE/RESPONSIVE ✅ Touch targets 44x44px minimum ✅ Zoom not disabled ✅ Content reflows at 320px ``` --- ## Key Takeaway > **Accessibility testing** ensures your app works for users with disabilities using assistive technologies. > **Responsive testing** ensures your app looks and works well on different screen sizes. > They **overlap** in areas like mobile accessibility, zoom behavior, and text reflow — so good teams test **both**.

text: ISO 26262: ASIL B compliance plugs types for a car
answer:
# ISO 26262 ASIL B Compliant Connector/Plug Types for Automotive Applications

## Overview

ASIL B (Automotive Safety Integrity Level B) requires a systematic capability of **SC3** and specific hardware/software architectural metrics. Connector selection must support these requirements.

---

## Key Compliance Requirements for ASIL B Connectors

| Parameter | ASIL B Requirement |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Random Hardware Failure | PMHF < 10⁻⁷/h |
| Single Point Fault Metric (SPFM) | ≥ 90% |
| Latent Fault Metric (LFM) | ≥ 60% |
| Diagnostic Coverage | Medium to High |

---

## Connector/Plug Types Used in ASIL B Applications

### 1. **High-Voltage (HV) Connectors**
- **Application:** EV/HEV battery systems, inverters, DC-DC converters
- **Examples:**
  - Rosenberger HV connectors (HVIL - High Voltage Interlock Loop)
  - TE Connectivity HDSCS (High Density Sealed Connector System)
  - Amphenol Torpedo series
- **Safety Features:**
  - HVIL circuit for shock protection detection
  - Touch-proof terminals
  - Coded/keyed to prevent mis-mating
  - IP67/IP69K rated

---

### 2. **Safety-Relevant ECU Connectors**
- **Application:** Airbag ECU, ABS/ESC modules, EPS, ADAS
- **Examples:**
  - Bosch Molex MX150
  - TE Connectivity Junior Power Timer (JPT)
  - Aptiv/Delphi GT series (GT 150, GT 280)
  - Yazaki 58-series
- **Safety Features:**
  - Secondary lock mechanisms (TPA - Terminal Position Assurance)
  - CPA (Connector Position Assurance) clips
  - Vibration resistance per LV214 standard

---

### 3. **Airbag Squib Connectors**
- **Application:** SRS (Supplemental Restraint Systems) — ASIL B/D
- **Examples:**
  - Aptiv Squib connectors
  - TE Connectivity AMPSEAL squib series
  - Tyco SMIA compliant connectors
- **Safety Features:**
  - Short-circuit protection
  - ESD protection integrated
  - SMIA (Squib Module Interface Agreement) compliant
  - Shorting clips to prevent inadvertent deployment

---

### 4. **Sealed/Waterproof Connectors**
- **Application:** Chassis, braking, steering systems
- **Examples:**
  - TE AMPSEAL 16
  - Molex CMC (Compact Micro Connector)
  - Sumitomo HX series
  - Deutsch DT/DTM series
- **Safety Features:**
  - IP67/IP68 sealing
  - Temperature range: -40°C to +125°C
  - Vibration tested per IEC 60068

---

### 5. **Fiber Optic Connectors (Safety Communication)**
- **Application:** MOST bus, LiDAR, camera safety systems
- **Examples:**
  - AVAGO MOST connectors
  - Rosenberger fiber optic automotive connectors
- **Safety Features:**
  - Immune to EMI/RFI
  - Signal integrity for safety communication paths

---

### 6. **PCB/Board-Level Safety Connectors**
- **Application:** Safety microcontroller boards, redundant circuits
- **Examples:**
  - Harting Har-Bus HM
  - TE Connectivity MULTIGIG RT series
  - Molex Micro-Fit 3.0
- **Safety Features:**
  - Redundant contact paths
  - Keying to prevent wrong insertion
  - Gold-plated contacts for reliability

---

## Standards Governing ASIL B Connector Selection

| Standard | Relevance |
|----------|-----------|
| **ISO 26262:2018 Part 8** | Hardware integration & connectors |
| **LV214** | German OEM connector qualification standard |
| **USCAR-2** | Performance standard for automotive connectors |
| **IEC 60664** | Insulation coordination |
| **ISO 17215 (SMIA)** | Squib connectors |
| **LV124 / LV148** | Electrical/electronic components testing |

---

## ASIL B Connector Design Checklist

```
✅ Dual-lock mechanisms (TPA + CPA)
✅ Keying/coding to prevent mis-mating
✅ Environmental sealing (IP6x)
✅ Vibration/shock qualification
✅ FMEA/FTA documented for connector failure modes
✅ Diagnostic feedback capability (HVIL, open-load detection)
✅ Temperature rating matching application
✅ Traceability & quality documentation (PPAP/APQP)
✅ Redundant contacts for safety-critical signals
```

---

## Supplier Ecosystem (ASIL B Qualified)

| Supplier | Notable Products |
|----------|----------------|
| **TE Connectivity** | AMPSEAL, JPT, HDSCS |
| **Aptiv/Delphi** | GT series, Squib |
| **Molex** | MX150, Micro-Fit |
| **Rosenberger** | HV, fiber optic |
| **Amphenol** | Torpedo, AT series |
| **Sumitomo** | HX, HW series |
| **Yazaki** | 58-series, YPC |

---

> **Note:** ASIL B compliance is a **system-level** property. Connectors themselves are **components** — full ASIL B compliance requires proper integration, FMEA documentation, and validation within the safety concept of the vehicle system.

text: ISO 26262:  Test Specification for a functional requirement "Companion App on Mobile Device shall only show a vehicle status update after a command only after this status update has been confirmed by vehicle". Write only a Test Procedure.
answer:
# Test Procedure: Vehicle Status Update Confirmation Before Display

**Test Procedure ID:** TP_APP_VSTATUS_001
**Related Requirement:** REQ_APP_VSTATUS_001
**ASIL Level:** To be defined per HARA

---

## Pre-conditions

1. Mobile device is powered on and the Companion App is installed and launched.
2. The Companion App is successfully paired and connected to the vehicle via the designated communication channel (e.g., Bluetooth / Telemobile / Cloud backend).
3. The vehicle ignition is in a defined known state (e.g., OFF or READY).
4. The vehicle ECU and telematics unit are operational and reachable.
5. A network/communication monitoring tool (e.g., packet sniffer, backend log tool) is active and able to capture messages exchanged between the App and the vehicle.
6. The current vehicle status displayed on the Companion App is in a known baseline state (e.g., doors locked, engine off).
7. Test engineer has access to a vehicle simulator or test bench capable of:
   - Receiving commands from the App.
   - Delaying, blocking, or manipulating confirmation messages back to the App.

---

## Test Steps

### Step 1 – Send a Command from the Companion App

| # | Action | Expected Reaction |
|---|--------|-------------------|
| 1.1 | On the Companion App, initiate a defined command (e.g., "Unlock Doors"). | The App sends the command message to the vehicle via the communication channel. The App UI shall display a **pending / in-progress** indicator and shall **NOT** update the vehicle status (e.g., shall NOT show "Doors Unlocked"). |
| 1.2 | Observe and record the App UI immediately after sending the command (before any vehicle response is received). | The status displayed on the App shall remain unchanged from the baseline state. No premature status update shall be shown. |

---

### Step 2 – Block / Delay the Vehicle Confirmation Message

| # | Action | Expected Reaction |
|---|--------|-------------------|
| 2.1 | Using the vehicle simulator or communication interception tool, **block** the vehicle confirmation message from being transmitted back to the App. | The vehicle physically executes the command (e.g., doors unlock at vehicle side) but the confirmation is not sent to the App. |
| 2.2 | Observe the Companion App UI for a defined observation period (e.g., 30 seconds or as defined in requirements). | The App shall **NOT** display an updated vehicle status (e.g., shall NOT show "Doors Unlocked"). The App shall continue to show the pending indicator or revert to the previous status. |
| 2.3 | Record the App UI state and any log entries. | No status update message shall appear in the App UI. Backend logs shall confirm no confirmation message was received by the App. |

---

### Step 3 – Release the Vehicle Confirmation Message

| # | Action | Expected Reaction |
|---|--------|-------------------|
| 3.1 | Release the previously blocked vehicle confirmation message, allowing the vehicle confirmation to be transmitted to the App. | The App receives the vehicle confirmation message. |
| 3.2 | Observe the Companion App UI immediately after the confirmation message is received. | The App shall **now** display the updated vehicle status (e.g., "Doors Unlocked") **only after** receiving the confirmation. |
| 3.3 | Record the timestamp of: (a) command sent, (b) confirmation received by App, (c) status update displayed on App UI. | The status update display event timestamp shall be **after** the confirmation receipt timestamp. No status update shall have occurred before this point. |

---

### Step 4 – Inject a Corrupted / Invalid Confirmation Message

| # | Action | Expected Reaction |
|---|--------|-------------------|
| 4.1 | Send a new command from the Companion App (e.g., "Lock Doors"). | App sends the command and shows pending state. |
| 4.2 | Using the vehicle simulator, inject a **corrupted, invalid, or spoofed** confirmation message (e.g., wrong message ID, invalid checksum, mismatched command reference). | The invalid message is transmitted to the App. |
| 4.3 | Observe the Companion App UI. | The App shall **NOT** accept the invalid confirmation and shall **NOT** update the vehicle status. The pending state or previous status shall be maintained. |

---

### Step 5 – Timeout Handling (No Confirmation Received)

| # | Action | Expected Reaction |
|---|--------|-------------------|
| 5.1 | Send a new command from the Companion App and ensure no confirmation message is ever returned (fully blocked). | App sends the command and shows pending state. |
| 5.2 | Wait for the timeout period to expire (as defined in the system specification). | After the defined timeout, the App shall **NOT** show a successful status update. The App shall display an appropriate error or timeout notification to the user (e.g., "Status update unavailable" or "Command could not be confirmed"). |
| 5.3 | Record the App UI state and log entries at timeout. | No false positive status update shall be displayed. Error handling behavior shall be consistent with requirements. |

---

### Step 6 – Successful End-to-End Nominal Flow (Sanity Check)

| # | Action | Expected Reaction |
|---|--------|-------------------|
| 6.1 | Remove all communication blocks and restore normal operating conditions. | System returns to normal communication state. |
| 6.2 | Send a command from the Companion App (e.g., "Unlock Doors") under nominal conditions. | The App sends the command. Vehicle executes the command and sends a valid confirmation. |
| 6.3 | Observe the Companion App UI after valid confirmation is received. | The App correctly displays the updated vehicle status **only after** receiving the valid vehicle confirmation. |
| 6.4 | Verify timestamps and logs confirm the sequence: Command Sent → Vehicle Executes → Confirmation Sent by Vehicle → Confirmation Received by App → Status Updated on App UI. | Sequence order is verified. No out-of-order status update is present. |

---

## Pass / Fail Criteria

| Criterion | Pass | Fail |
|-----------|------|------|
| App does not update status before confirmation is received | No status update shown prior to confirmation | Any status update displayed before confirmation receipt |
| App does not update status when confirmation is blocked | Status remains unchanged during block period | Status changes while confirmation is blocked |
| App does not update status on invalid/corrupted confirmation | Invalid confirmation is rejected; status unchanged | App accepts invalid message and updates status |
| App handles timeout without false status update | Error/timeout message shown; no false status update | App shows incorrect status after timeout |
| Nominal flow updates status correctly after confirmation | Status updated immediately upon valid confirmation | Status not updated or delayed without cause |

---

## Post-conditions

1. The Companion App is in a defined known state after test execution.
2. All communication monitoring tools are deactivated and logs are saved.
3. The vehicle simulator is reset to its default configuration.
4. All captured logs (App logs, backend logs, network traces) are archived with the test report.

---

## Deviation / Anomaly Handling

- Any unintended status update displayed **prior** to a valid vehicle confirmation shall be logged as a **safety-relevant defect** and reported immediately per the project defect management process.
- Any test step where the tool/environment prevents proper execution shall be documented as a test **deviation** and reviewed by the safety engineer.

text: ISO 26262: write a Test Specification for "Ethernet Interface shall be able to detect malfunctions of the Ethernet network and send alerts to HMIs and applications". Write only test cases
answer:
# Test Specification: Ethernet Interface Malfunction Detection and Alert Notification

---

## TEST CASES

---

### TC-ETH-001: Detection of Physical Link Loss

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-001 |
| **Title** | Detection of complete physical link disconnection |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-001 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Black-box / Fault Injection |

**Preconditions:**
- Ethernet interface is initialized and operational
- Link status is UP
- HMI and application connections are active

**Test Steps:**
1. Verify nominal Ethernet link is established and stable
2. Physically disconnect the Ethernet cable from the DUT
3. Start timer at moment of disconnection
4. Monitor internal diagnostic logs for fault detection event
5. Monitor HMI alert reception
6. Monitor application alert reception
7. Reconnect the Ethernet cable
8. Verify recovery and alert clearance

**Expected Results:**
- Link loss shall be detected within **≤ 100 ms** of disconnection
- Alert code `ETH_FAULT_LINK_DOWN` shall be generated
- HMI shall receive alert notification within **≤ 150 ms** of fault detection
- All registered applications shall receive alert notification within **≤ 150 ms** of fault detection
- Alert shall include: fault type, timestamp, interface ID
- Upon reconnection, recovery notification shall be sent to HMI and applications

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if all timing and content requirements are met; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-002: Detection of Excessive Packet Loss

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-002 |
| **Title** | Detection of packet loss exceeding defined threshold |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-002 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Black-box / Fault Injection |

**Preconditions:**
- Ethernet interface is operational
- Packet loss monitoring is enabled
- Baseline packet loss rate is < 0.01%

**Test Steps:**
1. Establish continuous traffic stream between DUT and test node
2. Record nominal packet loss rate (baseline)
3. Inject controlled packet loss at 1% rate using network impairment tool
4. Monitor for fault detection event
5. Increase packet loss to 5% and monitor response
6. Increase packet loss to 10% and monitor response
7. Remove packet loss injection and monitor recovery notification

**Expected Results:**
- No alert shall be generated at 1% packet loss (below threshold)
- Alert code `ETH_FAULT_PKT_LOSS_HIGH` shall be generated at ≥ 5% packet loss
- Alert severity shall escalate at 10% packet loss
- HMI and all registered applications shall receive alert within **≤ 200 ms**
- Alert shall include: current packet loss percentage, threshold value, interface ID
- Recovery notification shall be sent when packet loss returns below threshold

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if detection thresholds and notifications are correct; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-003: Detection of Network Latency Exceedance

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-003 |
| **Title** | Detection of network round-trip latency exceeding defined limits |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-003 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Black-box / Fault Injection |

**Preconditions:**
- Ethernet interface is operational
- Latency monitoring is active
- Nominal round-trip latency is < 1 ms

**Test Steps:**
1. Record baseline round-trip latency using test traffic
2. Inject artificial latency of 5 ms using network impairment tool
3. Monitor for fault detection event
4. Inject artificial latency of 10 ms
5. Monitor for fault detection event and severity change
6. Inject artificial latency of 50 ms
7. Monitor for fault detection event and severity escalation
8. Remove latency injection and verify recovery notification

**Expected Results:**
- Alert code `ETH_FAULT_LATENCY_HIGH` shall be generated when latency exceeds configured threshold (default: **10 ms**)
- No alert shall be generated at 5 ms latency injection (below threshold)
- Alert shall be generated within **≤ 500 ms** of threshold exceedance
- Alert severity shall escalate at 50 ms latency
- HMI and all registered applications shall receive alert
- Alert shall include: measured latency value, threshold, timestamp

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if thresholds are correctly detected and alerts delivered; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-004: Detection of CRC Error Rate Exceedance

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-004 |
| **Title** | Detection of abnormal CRC error rate on Ethernet frames |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-004 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Black-box / Fault Injection |

**Preconditions:**
- Ethernet interface is operational
- Frame integrity monitoring is active
- Nominal CRC error rate is 0

**Test Steps:**
1. Record baseline CRC error count (expected: 0)
2. Inject frames with corrupted CRC using traffic generator (rate: 10 frames/sec)
3. Monitor detection time and alert generation
4. Inject CRC errors at 100 frames/sec
5. Verify alert severity escalation
6. Stop CRC error injection
7. Verify recovery notification after error-free period

**Expected Results:**
- Alert code `ETH_FAULT_CRC_ERROR` shall be generated upon detection of CRC error rate above threshold
- Detection shall occur within **≤ 1 second** of threshold exceedance
- HMI and all registered applications shall be notified
- Alert shall include: CRC error count, error rate, interface ID, timestamp
- No false positive alerts shall occur during nominal operation

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if CRC error detection and alerts are correct; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-005: Detection of Duplicate IP / MAC Address Conflict

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-005 |
| **Title** | Detection of IP or MAC address conflict on the network |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-005 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL A |
| **Test Type** | Black-box / Fault Injection |

**Preconditions:**
- DUT Ethernet interface has a unique IP and MAC address assigned
- Network is operational with no address conflicts

**Test Steps:**
1. Connect a secondary test device to the network with an identical IP address as DUT
2. Monitor DUT for duplicate IP detection
3. Verify alert generation
4. Connect a secondary test device with an identical MAC address (if configurable in test environment)
5. Monitor DUT for duplicate MAC detection
6. Remove conflicting device
7. Verify recovery notification

**Expected Results:**
- Alert code `ETH_FAULT_IP_CONFLICT` shall be generated upon detection of duplicate IP address
- Alert code `ETH_FAULT_MAC_CONFLICT` shall be generated upon detection of duplicate MAC address
- Detection shall occur within **≤ 2 seconds**
- HMI and all registered applications shall receive alert
- Alert shall include: conflicting address, detection time, interface ID

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if conflicts are detected and correctly reported; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-006: Detection of Network Switch/Hub Failure

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-006 |
| **Title** | Detection of upstream network switch failure |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-006 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Fault Injection |

**Preconditions:**
- DUT is connected to network via managed switch
- Communication with peer nodes is nominal
- Switch health monitoring is active

**Test Steps:**
1. Verify nominal communication to all network peers
2. Power off the network switch
3. Start timer at switch power-off event
4. Monitor DUT for fault detection
5. Monitor HMI and application alert reception
6. Power on the switch after 30 seconds
7. Verify recovery notification

**Expected Results:**
- Loss of connectivity to all peers shall be detected within **≤ 500 ms**
- Alert code `ETH_FAULT_NETWORK_UNREACHABLE` shall be generated
- HMI and all registered applications shall receive alert within **≤ 1 second** of detection
- Alert shall include: list of unreachable nodes, timestamp, interface ID
- Recovery notification shall be sent upon switch restoration

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if network unreachability is detected and all parties notified; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-007: Detection of Bandwidth Saturation

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-007 |
| **Title** | Detection of network bandwidth saturation exceeding threshold |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-007 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL A |
| **Test Type** | Performance / Fault Injection |

**Preconditions:**
- Ethernet interface is 100 Mbps or 1 Gbps (as per system spec)
- Bandwidth monitoring is enabled
- Nominal utilization is < 30%

**Test Steps:**
1. Record baseline bandwidth utilization
2. Generate traffic load at 50% of interface capacity — verify no alert
3. Generate traffic load at 80% of interface capacity
4. Monitor for alert generation
5. Generate traffic load at 95% of interface capacity
6. Monitor for alert severity escalation
7. Reduce traffic to nominal levels
8. Verify recovery notification

**Expected Results:**
- No alert shall be generated at 50% utilization
- Alert code `ETH_FAULT_BW_SATURATION` shall be generated at ≥ 80% utilization
- Alert severity shall escalate at ≥ 95% utilization
- HMI and all registered applications shall receive alert within **≤ 500 ms**
- Alert shall include: current utilization percentage, threshold, interface ID
- Recovery notification shall be issued when utilization drops below threshold

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if saturation thresholds trigger correct alerts; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-008: Alert Delivery to Multiple HMI Instances

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-008 |
| **Title** | Verification that all registered HMI instances receive malfunction alerts |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-008 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Functional |

**Preconditions:**
- Minimum three HMI instances are registered and active
- Ethernet interface is operational

**Test Steps:**
1. Register three HMI instances (HMI-1, HMI-2, HMI-3) with the Ethernet interface
2. Inject a physical link fault (cable disconnection)
3. Monitor alert reception on HMI-1, HMI-2, and HMI-3 individually
4. Record timestamps of alert reception on each HMI
5. Deregister HMI-2
6. Inject another fault
7. Verify that only HMI-1 and HMI-3 receive the alert

**Expected Results:**
- All three registered HMIs shall receive alert for first fault injection
- Maximum delta between first and last HMI alert reception shall be **≤ 50 ms**
- After deregistration, HMI-2 shall NOT receive subsequent alerts
- HMI-1 and HMI-3 shall receive subsequent alert within timing requirements
- Alert content shall be identical across all receiving HMIs

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if all registered HMIs receive alerts and deregistered HMI does not; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-009: Alert Delivery to Multiple Application Instances

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-009 |
| **Title** | Verification that all registered application instances receive malfunction alerts |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-009 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Functional |

**Preconditions:**
- Minimum three application instances are registered
- Applications use defined alert callback/notification interface

**Test Steps:**
1. Register APP-1, APP-2, APP-3 with alert notification interface
2. Inject Ethernet fault (packet loss > threshold)
3. Monitor alert callback invocation on each application
4. Record timestamp of callback invocation per application
5. Verify alert data content for each application
6. Deregister APP-3
7. Inject a second fault
8. Verify that only APP-1 and APP-2 receive the alert

**Expected Results:**
- All three applications shall receive alert callback for first fault
- Maximum delta between first and last callback shall be **≤ 50 ms**
- Alert data structure shall contain: fault code, severity, timestamp, interface ID
- After deregistration, APP-3 shall NOT receive subsequent alerts
- No duplicate alert callbacks shall be delivered to any application

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if all conditions above are met; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-010: Alert Content Integrity and Format Validation

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-010 |
| **Title** | Validation of alert message content, format, and mandatory fields |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-010 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Functional / Content Validation |

**Preconditions:**
- Ethernet interface is operational
- Alert logging is enabled

**Test Steps:**
1. Inject each of the following faults sequentially:
   - Physical link loss
   - Packet loss threshold exceedance
   - Latency threshold exceedance
   - CRC error threshold exceedance
   - Bandwidth saturation
2. Capture alert messages delivered to HMI and applications for each fault
3. Parse and validate content of each captured alert message
4. Verify mandatory fields are present and correctly populated
5. Verify alert severity encoding is correct for each fault type
6. Verify timestamp accuracy against system reference time (tolerance: ± 10 ms)

**Expected Results:**
Each alert message shall contain the following mandatory fields:
- `fault_code` — valid enumerated fault identifier
- `severity` — INFO / WARNING / ERROR / CRITICAL (correctly assigned)
- `timestamp` — UTC or system time, accurate within ± 10 ms
- `interface_id` — valid Ethernet interface identifier
- `description` — human-readable fault description
- `detected_value` — measured parameter that triggered alert
- `threshold_value` — configured threshold
- No mandatory field shall be NULL or empty
- Alert format shall comply with defined ICD (Interface Control Document)

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if all mandatory fields are present, correctly formatted, and accurate; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-011: No False Positive Alerts During Nominal Operation

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-011 |
| **Title** | Verification of absence of spurious alerts during nominal network operation |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-011 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Negative / Stability |

**Preconditions:**
- Ethernet interface is fully operational
- Network conditions are within all nominal parameters
- HMI and applications are registered and monitoring

**Test Steps:**
1. Establish and confirm nominal network operation
2. Run continuous nominal traffic for **60 minutes**
3. Monitor HMI and all applications for any unsolicited alerts
4. Log any alert received during the monitoring period
5. Verify network parameters remained within nominal bounds throughout

**Expected Results:**
- Zero malfunction alerts shall be generated during nominal 60-minute operation
- HMI shall receive zero fault notifications
- All applications shall receive zero fault notifications
- No `ETH_FAULT_*` event shall appear in diagnostic logs

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if zero false positive alerts are generated; FAIL if any spurious alert occurs

---

### TC-ETH-012: Alert Generation During DUT Startup and Initialization

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-012 |
| **Title** | Correct alert behavior during Ethernet interface initialization phase |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-012 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Boundary / Functional |

**Preconditions:**
- DUT is powered off
- Network is in operational state

**Test Steps:**
1. Power on the DUT with Ethernet cable connected
2. Monitor for any spurious alerts during initialization phase
3. Record time at which Ethernet interface transitions to OPERATIONAL state
4. Power on the DUT with Ethernet cable disconnected
5. Monitor for correct fault alert generation after initialization completes
6. Connect Ethernet cable after initialization
7. Verify recovery notification

**Expected Results:**
- No `ETH_FAULT_LINK_DOWN` alert shall be generated during initialization phase (before interface reaches OPERATIONAL state)
- `ETH_FAULT_LINK_DOWN` alert shall be generated within **≤ 500 ms** of interface reaching OPERATIONAL state if link is absent
- HMI and applications shall be notified after interface is OPERATIONAL
- Recovery alert shall be sent upon successful link establishment

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if alerts are suppressed during init and correctly generated post-init; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-013: Alert Behavior Under Intermittent Link Flapping

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-013 |
| **Title** | Alert debounce and stability under rapid link state changes (link flapping) |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-013 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Robustness / Fault Injection |

**Preconditions:**
- Ethernet interface is operational
- Alert debounce mechanism is configured (debounce time: 200 ms)

**Test Steps:**
1. Simulate link flapping at 10 Hz (100 ms ON / 100 ms OFF) for 10 seconds
2. Count number of alerts generated and delivered to HMI and applications
3. Simulate link flapping at 1 Hz (500 ms ON / 500 ms OFF) for 10 seconds
4. Count number of alerts generated and delivered
5. Introduce single clean link loss of 5 seconds duration
6. Verify single alert is generated

**Expected Results:**
- At 10 Hz flapping: alert storm prevention shall limit alerts to ≤ 5 alerts over 10 seconds
- At 1 Hz flapping: each stable DOWN state shall generate exactly one alert; each recovery shall generate exactly one recovery notification
- For single clean 5-second link loss: exactly one fault alert and one recovery notification shall be generated
- No alert buffer overflow or memory fault shall occur
- HMI and applications shall not be flooded with duplicate alerts

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if debounce and storm prevention behave as specified; FAIL otherwise

---

### TC-ETH-014: Alert Delivery Verification When HMI is Temporarily Unavailable

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Test Case ID** | TC-ETH-014 |
| **Title** | Verification of alert buffering and delivery when HMI reconnects after temporary unavailability |
| **Requirement Reference** | REQ-ETH-014 |
| **ASIL Level** | ASIL B |
| **Test Type** | Robustness / Fault Injection |

**Preconditions:**
- HMI is registered and connected
- Alert buffering is configured (buffer size: as per system spec)

**Test Steps:**
1. Disconnect HMI communication channel (simulate HMI unavailability)
2. Inject three distinct Ethernet faults while HMI is unavailable
3. Record fault types and timestamps
4. Reconnect HMI communication channel
5. Monitor HMI for receipt of buffered alerts
6. Verify all three alerts are delivered after reconnection
7. Verify correct ordering and content of delivered alerts

**Expected Results:**
- Ethernet Interface shall buffer fault alerts while HMI is unavailable
- Upon HMI reconnection, all buffered alerts shall be delivered within **≤ 1 second**
- Alerts shall be delivered in chronological order (FIFO)
- Alert content shall match originally injected fault details
- No alert shall be lost due to HMI temporary unavailability

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** PASS if all buffered alerts are correctly delivered upon HMI reconnection; FAIL otherwise

---

*Document Reference: TS-ETH-MALFUNCTION-001*
*ASIL Classification: ASIL B (system-level)*
*Prepared in accordance with ISO 26262-6*

text: ISO 26262: Technical requirements for functional requirement "Secure Network Functionality shall be able to block incoming signals that are not coming from the correct sender."
answer:
# ISO 26262: Technical Requirements for Functional Safety

## Functional Requirement
**"Secure Network Functionality shall be able to block incoming signals that are not coming from the correct sender."**

---

## 1. Safety Context & Classification

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Functional Requirement ID** | FR-NET-001 |
| **Related Safety Goal** | Prevent unauthorized/malicious signals from causing unintended vehicle behavior |
| **Applicable ASIL** | ASIL B–D (depending on safety goal decomposition) |
| **Relevant Norm** | ISO 26262-4/5/6, ISO 21434 (cybersecurity co-engineering) |

---

## 2. Technical Safety Requirements (TSRs)

### 2.1 Sender Authentication & Signal Validation

| Req. ID | Technical Requirement | ASIL |
|---|---|---|
| TSR-NET-001 | The system **shall** verify the sender identity of every received network message using an authenticated identifier (e.g., MAC address, node ID, cryptographic signature) before processing. | ASIL C |
| TSR-NET-002 | The system **shall** maintain a trusted sender list (whitelist) containing all valid authorized sender identifiers per communication channel. | ASIL B |
| TSR-NET-003 | The system **shall** reject and discard any message whose sender identifier does not match an entry in the trusted sender list. | ASIL C |
| TSR-NET-004 | The system **shall** generate a diagnostic fault event upon detection of an unauthorized sender, within **≤10 ms** of message receipt. | ASIL B |
| TSR-NET-005 | The system **shall** support Message Authentication Codes (MAC) or equivalent cryptographic mechanism to validate signal authenticity at the receiver node. | ASIL C |

---

### 2.2 Signal Integrity & Anti-Spoofing

| Req. ID | Technical Requirement | ASIL |
|---|---|---|
| TSR-NET-006 | The system **shall** implement a freshness counter or timestamp mechanism to detect replayed messages from unauthorized senders. | ASIL C |
| TSR-NET-007 | The system **shall** detect message injection attacks by validating message sequence numbers against expected ranges, with a fault coverage ≥ 90%. | ASIL B |
| TSR-NET-008 | The system **shall** not propagate any signal to safety-relevant actuators or controllers until sender authentication is confirmed. | ASIL D |
| TSR-NET-009 | The bus guardian or gateway node **shall** independently verify sender authorization before forwarding safety-critical messages. | ASIL C |

---

### 2.3 Blocking Mechanism

| Req. ID | Technical Requirement | ASIL |
|---|---|---|
| TSR-NET-010 | The system **shall** implement a hardware-supported firewall or gateway filter capable of blocking unauthorized messages at the physical/data link layer. | ASIL B |
| TSR-NET-011 | The blocking function **shall** operate independently of the application software layer to prevent bypassing through software faults (independence requirement). | ASIL C |
| TSR-NET-012 | The blocking latency **shall** not exceed **5 ms** from detection of unauthorized sender to signal suppression under all operating conditions. | ASIL C |
| TSR-NET-013 | The system **shall** ensure blocked signals are logged in a non-volatile fault memory with timestamp, sender ID, and bus channel identifier. | ASIL B |
| TSR-NET-014 | The blocking function **shall** remain operational during degraded mode (partial power loss, ECU reset) to prevent window-of-vulnerability during transitions. | ASIL C |

---

### 2.4 Fail-Safe Behavior

| Req. ID | Technical Requirement | ASIL |
|---|---|---|
| TSR-NET-015 | Upon failure of the sender authentication mechanism itself, the system **shall** transition to a safe state (e.g., reject all messages / halt signal propagation) — **fail-secure default**. | ASIL D |
| TSR-NET-016 | The system **shall** monitor the health of the authentication module with a watchdog mechanism at a diagnostic interval of **≤ 10 ms**. | ASIL C |
| TSR-NET-017 | A failure of the blocking function **shall** be detectable with a diagnostic coverage (DC) of **≥ 97%** (target metric for ASIL D hardware). | ASIL D |
| TSR-NET-018 | The system **shall** alert the vehicle system supervisor (e.g., central gateway) of any blocking function failure within **≤ 20 ms**. | ASIL B |

---

### 2.5 Configuration & Key Management

| Req. ID | Technical Requirement | ASIL |
|---|---|---|
| TSR-NET-019 | The trusted sender list **shall** only be modifiable through an authenticated and authorized configuration interface (e.g., secure bootloader, HSM-controlled OTA). | ASIL B |
| TSR-NET-020 | Cryptographic keys used for sender authentication **shall** be stored in a Hardware Security Module (HSM) and **shall not** be accessible to application-level software. | ASIL C |
| TSR-NET-021 | Key update procedures **shall** maintain blocking functionality continuity — no interruption of the blocking function during key rotation. | ASIL B |

---

## 3. Hardware Technical Safety Requirements

| Req. ID | Technical Requirement | ASIL |
|---|---|---|
| HTSR-NET-001 | The network controller hardware **shall** support hardware-level message filtering with SPFM ≥ 90% (Single-Point Fault Metric). | ASIL C |
| HTSR-NET-002 | The HSM used for authentication **shall** have a proven-in-use or certified safety integrity level consistent with the target ASIL. | ASIL C |
| HTSR-NET-003 | The gateway ECU hardware **shall** implement redundant communication path monitoring to detect hardware faults in the blocking circuitry. | ASIL B |

---

## 4. Software Technical Safety Requirements

| Req. ID | Technical Requirement | ASIL |
|---|---|---|
| STSR-NET-001 | The authentication software module **shall** be developed in accordance with ISO 26262-6 at the required ASIL level (ASIL B/C/D as applicable). | ASIL C |
| STSR-NET-002 | The blocking software function **shall** be spatially and temporally isolated from QM software partitions (memory protection unit enforcement). | ASIL C |
| STSR-NET-003 | The software **shall** implement defensive programming measures (input validation, range checks) on all received sender IDs before processing. | ASIL B |
| STSR-NET-004 | Code coverage for the authentication and blocking modules **shall** meet **MC/DC (Modified Condition/Decision Coverage)** criteria per ISO 26262-6 Table 12. | ASIL C/D |

---

## 5. Verification & Validation Requirements

| V&V Requirement | Method | Acceptance Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| Verify blocking of unauthorized sender | Fault injection testing on CAN/Ethernet bus | 100% of unauthorized messages blocked |
| Verify detection latency ≤ 5 ms | Hardware timing measurement | P99 latency < 5 ms |
| Verify fail-secure behavior on auth module failure | Component fault injection | System enters safe state in ≤ 20 ms |
| Verify trusted sender list integrity | Security penetration testing | No unauthorized modification possible |
| Verify no propagation to safety actuators | End-to-end signal tracing | Zero propagation events observed |

---

## 6. Traceability Summary

```
Safety Goal (SG-NET-01)
    └── Functional Safety Requirement (FR-NET-001)
            ├── TSR-NET-001 to TSR-NET-021  (System Level)
            ├── HTSR-NET-001 to HTSR-NET-003 (Hardware Level)
            └── STSR-NET-001 to STSR-NET-004 (Software Level)
                        └── V&V Requirements
```

---

> **Note:** These requirements should be co-reviewed with **ISO/SAE 21434** (cybersecurity) requirements, as sender spoofing is both a **safety** and **cybersecurity** concern. A TARA (Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment) under ISO 21434 should be aligned with the HARA under ISO 26262 to ensure consistent treatment.
